review_rationale: Fourteenth Amendment Section 1 establishes specific citizenship and legal protections against state action; it is not equivalent to the Declaration's universal equality proposition. Ratified in 1868.
Both texts articulate governmental purposes involving liberty. Retain only as historical-context comparison; the Preamble independently grants no governmental power.

Article I Section 7 establishes presentment, qualified presidential veto, congressional reconsideration, override, and consequences for inaction. Structural comparison only; no historical causation established.
Article IV Section 4 does not directly regulate the governor-assent obstruction described in this grievance. The proposed pairing is insufficiently specific.
Article I Section 2 establishes an elected House, not an unrestricted right to representation. Original apportionment exclusions and inequalities must be acknowledged.
Article I Section 5 regulates congressional proceedings and adjournment location, but does not comprehensively prohibit coercive legislative convening.
Article I Section 2 establishes biennial House elections but does not expressly prohibit executive dissolution of legislative bodies.
